newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian exports hit by rupee appreciation -minister.
newsitem.headline: Indian exports hit by rupee appreciation -minister.

text.p: Indian Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah said on Monday that the recent appreciation of the rupee is affecting the country's exports "to some extent".
Ramaiah was asked after addressing a business seminar in the capital if exports were affected by the appreciation of the Indian currency against the U.S. dollar.
"Of course to some extent. Also because neighbouring countries like Pakistan and others have devalued," he told reporters. "So competition is increasing."
Ramaiah said the rate of export growth in 1997/98 (April-March) will be higher than in 1996/97, when foreign sales rose 4.01 percent to $33.11 billion.
"This year it will be definitely more than that," Ramaiah said when asked if the export growth rate this fiscal year will top last year's.
The Commerce Ministry reported on Friday that exports fell by 0.95 percent to $8.13 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 1997/98 from $8.21 billion a year earlier.
Exports in June grew by just 2.53 percent to $2.66 billion from $2.59 billion in the same month in 1996.
Ramaiah said the government was reviewing the reasons for the slowdown in exports and would soon suggest steps to spur foreign sales.
Asked whether he was in favour of a devaluation of the rupee, Ramaiah said: "No. I can't do it."
"I have to examine all issues concerning the country, not just one side of it," he added.
Ramaiah said that a devaluation would increase the cost of petroleum, fertiliser and edible oil imports, among the nation's main imports.
